paras: The killing of an unknown tramp at Barnard, Missouri, took place in April 1882, when an armed party hunted down and shot a man accused of killing Charles C. Alkire. Accounts disagreed on whether the killers were townspeople who burned him out of a woodpile or a sheriff's posse trying to arrest him. The story ran in papers across the country within days, and one North Carolina weekly counted it among the West's mob killings.

According to a St. Louis dispatch, people near Barnard, close to Maryville, had been annoyed by an unknown "crazy" tramp who went about begging. The National Associated Press added that he imagined himself one of the James boys and had lived in the woods for some weeks, stopping people on the road.

A constable and several men, Alkire among them, went to arrest the tramp, who fired a revolver and struck Alkire in the neck, severing the jugular vein; Alkire died soon after. A St. Joseph dispatch told it differently, saying only that the tramp had murdered Alkire "in cold blood." The reported date varies between Monday night, April 17, and the night of April 18.

In the St. Joseph account, "the citizens" chased the tramp to a lot of cordwood where they could not reach him and decided to "blaze him out." They threw bottles of petroleum against the woodpile, followed by lighted cotton, and when the heat drove him out he was shot, with fifteen bullet holes found in him. The Associated Press version instead had the sheriff and his men besiege him in the woodpile and kill him after a battle lasting nearly all day, in which he was wounded seven times.
No papers or letters identifying the dead man were found, and he was thought to have been insane. No report of an inquest or of any official inquiry into his death appears in the coverage.

Two competing wire stories, one from St. Joseph and one from St. Louis, appeared on April 20 in papers from Salt Lake City and Cheyenne to Wheeling, St. Paul and Memphis. Headlines cast the dead man as the wrongdoer: "A Tramp-Murderer Killed" in Wheeling, "A Murderous Lunatic" in Omaha, and "A Murderer Hunted Like a Wild Beast" in Los Angeles. The St. Paul Daily Globe headed the item "One Tramp the Less."

Later news briefs boiled the story down to a line or two, saying either that a sheriff's posse killed him while trying to arrest him or that "the inhabitants hunted him down and killed him." On May 3 the Raleigh Farmer and Mechanic reprinted the St. Joseph dispatch in a column headed "Western Mobs," which counted more than a dozen men hanged by mobs in the North and West in the past month. None of the reports gave the tramp's race.

The St. Joseph dispatch credited the killing to the citizens, while the St. Louis and Associated Press dispatches said the sheriff and his deputies killed the tramp while trying to arrest him. The two versions also differed on how many times he was hit, fifteen against seven.

bases: Every account has an armed party pursue and kill a man accused of shooting Alkire; the St. Louis and Associated Press versions make it a sheriff's posse (A2, A3, A11), the St. Joseph version a turnout of citizens (A1, A15).

A group killed the tramp after he was accused of killing Alkire (A1, A2, A3), but whether it acted without legal authority is disputed: the St. Joseph dispatch describes citizens who burned him out and shot him (A1, A9), while the St. Louis and Associated Press dispatches describe a sheriff and deputies killing him while trying to arrest him (A2, A3, A12). No report gives the tramp's race.

Two independent wire versions (St. Joseph, A1; St. Louis, A2) and a National Associated Press dispatch (A3) agree that a tramp shot Alkire near Barnard and was then hunted down and killed, though they differ on who killed him and how.

accounts.label: St. Joseph dispatch
accounts.gist: A tramp murdered Alkire 'in cold blood'; the citizens ran him to cover in cordwood, burned him out with petroleum and lighted cotton, and riddled him with fifteen bullets. He carried no papers and was thought insane.

accounts.label: St. Louis dispatch
accounts.gist: A crazy begging tramp had annoyed people near Barnard; a constable's party including Alkire went to arrest him and he shot Alkire in the neck; the sheriff and deputies hunted him and killed him.

accounts.label: National Associated Press
accounts.gist: The tramp, who imagined himself one of the James boys, shot Alkire of a constable's posse; the sheriff and men besieged him in a pile of wood and killed him after a battle of nearly all day, wounding him seven times.

framing.detail: Papers ran the wire versions with headlines casting the dead man as murderer and lunatic ('A Tramp-Murderer Killed', 'A Murderous Lunatic') and offered no criticism of his killers.
The St. Paul Daily Globe headed the story 'One Tramp the Less'.
The Raleigh Farmer and Mechanic grouped the St. Joseph dispatch with hangings in a 'Western Mobs' roundup counting mob killings in the North and West.
